scope: Read-only performance review of saved runtime measurements and W01ResumeCyclesR2.java. No active simulation, process allocation, numerical control, monitor or controller was changed. Standalone review and interval-breakdown JSON only.
conclusion: The short sample shows low average GPU utilization while the single owned solver process uses about one CPU core. CPU-side reporting on derived parts is a documented, plausible source of serial work. This does not establish the dominant cause or promise a speedup. Optimize measured wall seconds per physical second, not GPU utilization percentage.

limitations: GPU sample is about 21 seconds, not a cycle-average profile.
Sixteen separate HF CPU processes were observed using about 0.9 cores each; their allocation and execution must remain untouched.
Clock and power variation do not by themselves prove throttling, nor does low GPU utilization prove insufficient CPU workers.
No actual enabled-monitor or scene-update inventory was obtained from the active solver; no API attachment was made.

timing_interpretation.history_clock: wall_s is sampled after the solve and early guard reports, before much of the remaining postprocessing. Adjacent-row differences include previous-row output work plus the following solve.
timing_interpretation.trace_confound: This window includes deliberate AMG LOW logging for upcoming physical times 0.605–0.635. Thirty intervals classified only as AMG trace average 2.81628 s; overlaps are classified as output. Do not extrapolate trace cost to the entire run.
timing_interpretation.output_correlation: A 8.797254 s interval follows relative step 500, which performs full local CSV, outlet export, checkpoint and monitor exports. A 7.388882 s interval follows step 450, an outlet-export step. The other two outlet-export intervals are near ordinary cost, so export cadence alone does not explain every spike.
timing_interpretation.causality: These are temporal associations from one live run, not an A/B attribution.

primary_documentation.title: GPGPU Functionality
primary_documentation.finding: The installed version enables selected reports on GPU when monitored during solution iteration. Supported report parts are regions, boundaries and parts, excluding derived parts. Reports not GPU-enabled execute on CPU. Force, min/max, sum and integral families appear in the supported-or-low-penalty list, but that list does not override the derived-part restriction.
primary_documentation.implication: ThresholdPart interface-CFL and outlet-column sums, and PlaneSection gauges, warrant profiling. A report family name alone is insufficient to assume GPU execution.

primary_documentation.title: GPGPU Functionality
primary_documentation.finding: Primitive, derived and most user-defined field functions are GPU enabled; some user-defined functions still run on CPU and may incur a penalty.
primary_documentation.implication: Do not label all analytic-wave or user-defined fields CPU-only without measurement or explicit support evidence.

primary_documentation.title: Running Simulations with GPGPU
primary_documentation.finding: For fully GPU-enabled operations the guide recommends matching CPU processes to GPU cards to avoid oversubscription. If CPU operations are present it suggests considering more CPU processes, using multiples of GPU count.
primary_documentation.implication: One GPU plus one CPU process is not inherently misconfigured. A separate one-to-two process benchmark is defensible if reporting/profile evidence warrants it; more processes are not an automatic improvement.

primary_documentation.title: GPGPU Computation
primary_documentation.finding: The platform-specific text says MPS is not relevant for NVIDIA GPUs on Windows; no automatic MPS handling is performed and the nomps qualifier is ignored.
primary_documentation.implication: Do not prescribe Linux MPS setup on this Windows machine.

primary_documentation.title: Controlling Graphics Performance
primary_documentation.finding: Rendering options govern graphics demand and have separate rendering-platform behavior.
primary_documentation.implication: Stored scene existence is not evidence of continuous rendering. Audit open scene and update state before attributing cost to the twelve stored views.

source_code_findings.fact: The continuation preserves source reports/monitors and creates new reports and monitors. The only blanket disable targets names beginning Short_ and containing Yplus.
source_code_findings.uncertainty: Potential duplicates are inferred from code; actual source monitor inventory and update frequencies must be recorded before disabling anything.
source_code_findings.safe_action: In a new checkpoint-copy benchmark inventory all monitor names, report bindings, inputs and update modes; disable only verified obsolete duplicate diagnostic monitors, retaining current force, native phase, outlet phase and guard reporting.

source_code_findings.fact: Two new outlet-column MassImbalance sums on an x-threshold explicitly update every inner iteration. max() also creates a monitor for the dynamic alpha-threshold interface CFL. The default frequency of that max monitor is not explicitly set.
source_code_findings.uncertainty: The exact per-step cost and default max-monitor cadence have not been measured.
source_code_findings.safe_action: First measure. If interface-CFL monitor proves repeated and unused by stopping criteria/required inner evidence, benchmark disabling only that automatic monitor while preserving the same report evaluation in every macro timestep guard. Do not change outlet/native inner histories in the first optimization.

source_code_findings.fact: Every step evaluates each mixture flux report in the net/inflow loop, then fetches the same report again for the phase-flux CSV.
source_code_findings.uncertainty: The second getter may return cached data, so duplicate source calls do not prove duplicate reduction cost.
source_code_findings.safe_action: A separate candidate may cache the first finite mixture-flux values in a local array for that same completed step and write those exact values. Validate identical output and budget; do not combine this with a monitor benchmark.

source_code_findings.fact: Analytic whole-domain inventory is evaluated each step; seven actual/reference plane gauges every ten steps; outlet cell/face exports every fifty; full local CSV and checkpoint every five hundred; native/outlet inner history is retained.
source_code_findings.safe_action: Preserve live scientific data and guards. Profile sections before reducing nonessential export frequency; the rare checkpoint overhead is a preservation cost, not a reason to remove checkpoints.

source_code_findings.fact: Each step opens/appends amg_cycle_counts.csv using cumulative API counters already shown unreliable for achieved linear convergence; actual LOW logs remain the established evidence.
source_code_findings.safe_action: Removing or buffering this non-authoritative auxiliary output is a later independent low-risk candidate, not a claimed large speedup.

source_code_findings.fact: Twelve native inspection scenes and two streamline parts are created; code does not prove that these are rendered every step.
source_code_findings.safe_action: Do not delete or blame scenes solely from their presence. If an actual open auto-refresh scene is found, benchmark its refresh cadence separately while retaining saved native views.

controlled_benchmark.sequencing: Keep current run intact. At an already planned, completed and hash-verified non-guard-failed checkpoint boundary, preserve the source and create new unique baseline/candidate folders. Never launch beside the active owned GPU controller; verify queue and process release first.
controlled_benchmark.first_step: Use identical reporting-only timing instrumentation in both copies to time solve, guard reports, mass/flux reductions, gauges, output extraction and saves. Inventory monitors without mutating numerical fields. The first perturbation should be one verified redundant monitor group or one redundant getter cache, not a bundle of changes.
settings_fixed: Mesh, domain, wave, boundary conditions and physical checkpoint state
GPU count 1 and CPU process count 1 for reporting benchmark
SO time scheme, dt, inner iterations, AMG tolerances/caps, URFs and VOF settings
50 m/s, alpha, finite field, mass/time/resource and source-identity guards
Native phase and BDF2 diagnostics with unchanged 0.01% review threshold; existing exploratory exception remains explicitly labelled
Current force/component/gauge histories, checkpoint policy and complete-cycle repeatability policy
controlled_benchmark.length: 20 warm-up steps then at least 100 matched measured steps; use a common physical window after the temporary 0.605–0.635 AMG trace. Preserve equivalent output/checkpoint cadence and report event-free and inclusive timing separately.
compare: Mean and median seconds/step and seconds per physical second, including and excluding scheduled I/O events
Timed solver/report/output sections, GPU activity, clocks/power and owned CPU time
Exact timestamps/sample counts and all guard outcomes
CD, CL, pressure/viscous drag, gauge elevation, native water/air error, BDF2+flux, speed/phase bounds against baseline at matched times
controlled_benchmark.numerical_equivalence: For a reporting-only change on the same one-process decomposition, require bitwise equality where feasible and otherwise tightly bounded roundoff differences. Any systematic trajectory or diagnostic change rejects a pure-performance claim. Do not use performance optimization to erase a previously exceeded mass criterion.
controlled_benchmark.noise_control: The separate HF job remains untouched. Record its concurrent CPU load and total memory pressure. If improvement is small versus observed run variability, regard it as inconclusive; a bounded A/B/A repeat is justified only then.
controlled_benchmark.second_independent_option: If profiling shows CPU-side work remains dominant, test one to two CPU processes on the same GPU from the same checkpoint, with all reporting/numerics fixed and a new attempt ID. Verify fields and force/gauge agreement because decomposition can alter floating-point ordering. Do not combine with reporting changes or alter the separate HF ranks.
controlled_benchmark.adoption: Adopt only after a sustained measured wall-time improvement exceeding measurement variability and unchanged scientific/guard evidence. GPU percentage alone is not an acceptance metric.

no_actions_taken: No changes to the separate HF session
